question: You will see one image. Which of these is it most likely to be? (a) a frame from a top-budget film, a AAA game cinematic or a cinema nature documentary, (b) a stock photograph, (c) a seed catalog or textbook picture, (d) amateur generated art, (e) a real-time web 3D demo. Answer with one letter, a confidence from 0 to 100, and the one thing that most influenced your answer.

votes.answer: a, 72/100. The fog-filtered sunrise creates a deliberately cinematic depth separation around the foreground bud.

e, 82, the combination of real-time atmospheric post-processing (fog, sun glow, and screen-space depth of field) with visibly lightweight 3D plant geometry—faceted leaf silhouettes, simple tubular stem/petiole meshes, and instanced low-poly background stalks.

a — confidence 55. The biggest factor was the quality of the CG: the fine backlit hairs along the stems and leaf edges, the volumetric fog with depth falloff, and the hazy sun all look like an offline, film-grade render with cinematic framing. That is too polished for amateur art or a real-time web demo, and the hair is too uniform for a real stock photo.
e, 76/100. The repeated, nearly identical plant silhouettes in the background look like instanced 3D assets.
b, 74, centered isolated frost-covered sunflower in fog, composed as a sellable beauty still rather than a narrative film frame or a render
